items.title: How fast does one label multiply a metric into a storage problem?
items.description: The L2 table starts from a request-count metric already labeled by statusCode and route — about 400 time series. Drag how many distinct values a new label (like userId or sessionId) can take to see how many time series that single label multiplies the metric into.

params.name: labelDistinctValues
params.label: Distinct values of the new label

items.compute: const baseSeries = 400; const totalSeries = baseSeries * params.labelDistinctValues; return { totalSeries };

items.title: How much does sampling actually cut, once every failure is still kept?
items.description: payment-service logs 40M lines/day at roughly a 2.1% error rate (from L1's example). Failures are always kept in full; drag the sample rate applied only to successful requests to see how many lines per day actually get stored.
items.compute: const totalLines = 40000000; const errorRate = 0.021; const errorLines = Math.round(totalLines * errorRate); const successLines = totalLines - errorLines; const sampledSuccessLines = Math.round(successLines * (params.sampleRatePercent / 100)); const linesStored = errorLines + sampledSuccessLines; return { linesStored };
